title: The agents ran on their own tonight; three decisions for the morning
when: 2 November 2026, 22:35 UTC (scheduled wake; since brief 3, 20:30 UTC)
headline: The schedules work: the journalist wrote the day's newsletter, the SGit agent made its first run, and the dev agent cut the build from 3.3 to 0.45 seconds, all without anyone asking. The designer has the home page (WS-103) and every person's conductor now has the briefing article. Three things need you, best before the 13:00 stand-up: a name collision in the session you started at 22:27, the print order's deadline and ceiling, and how vault keys get sealed.

for_you.detail: Its title is dashboard@web-summit.dinis, but its first commit (22:28, its key and people/dinis/agents.json) is signed conductor@web-summit.dinis, which is this session's name, and it notes the dashboard agent as not started. for_you.ask: The print order: artwork deadline, fallback and ceiling
for_you.detail: Silvio's procurement agent: 2 of 7 printers have replied; one cannot make Friday, one quoted only white, black or grey, if paid with final artwork today. On tomorrow's 13:00 agenda.

for_you.ask: How do vault keys reach an agent's key? (WS-102)
for_you.detail: pki-agent seal only seals to keys in the pki.sgit.ai register, but since this evening agent keys are only published on the keys page. Until one way is picked, nobody can reach L6 (the vaults).
options: a small seal tool that reads the recipient from data/keys.json (the trust is the push)
register every agent key on pki.sgit.ai too, and you confirm each
for_you.recommend: The seal tool: it matches the corrected method, and the dev agent can build it tomorrow.
